comp2.title: Building Pakistan's capability in satellite navigation and PNT
comp2.description: The GNSS Research Lab provides a focused environment for research, academic development and technology-oriented problem solving in Global Navigation Satellite Systems.

comp3.title: The GNSS Research Lab was established

cards.title: At the Institute of Space Technology, Islamabad (IST)
Under the National Center of GIS & Space Applications (NCGSA)
To strengthen Pakistan's research and technological capacity in Positioning, Navigation and Timing (PNT)

history.title: History
history.description: Its foundation was built upon IST's pioneering MS in Global Navigation Satellite Systems, launched in Spring 2014 in accordance with the curriculum developed by the United Nations Office for Outer Space Affairs. As Pakistan's only specialized GNSS degree programme, it created a growing need for dedicated infrastructure to support advanced education, experimentation and applied research in satellite navigation.

platformCards.title: The Lab was therefore developed as an integrated research platform for:

cards.title: GNSS receivers, signal processing, precise positioning, augmentation systems
Software-defined navigation, sensor integration, ionospheric monitoring and resilient PNT
Its facilities support academic programmes, research projects, technology development
Field experimentation and professional capacity building

gnssContributions.title: GNSS Contributions
gnssContributions.description: Today, the GNSS Research Lab contributes to indigenous space capability and the practical application of satellite navigation in :

cards.title: GNSS contributes in various domains like Surveying, transportation, telecommunications, agriculture
Disaster management, environmental monitoring, infrastructure development and national security
Its activities also support Pakistan's National Space Policy, the URAAN Pakistan 5Es framework, and relevant United Nations Sustainable Development Goals

comp4.title: Vision
comp4.description: To position the GNSS Research Lab as a nationally leading and internationally recognized center of excellence in satellite navigation, precise positioning, resilient Positioning, Navigation and Timing (PNT), and space-weather research. The Lab aims to strengthen indigenous technological capability, develop skilled human resources, and deliver GNSS-enabled solutions that support sustainable development, resilient infrastructure, environmental monitoring, smart mobility, agriculture, disaster management, and national strategic priorities.

comp5.title: Alignment with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals
comp5.description: The GNSS Research Lab contributes United Nations Sustainable Development Goals through research, technology development, academic programmes, observatory services, capacity building, and national and international collaboration.

cards.title: Zero Hunger
cards.description: The Lab supports GNSS-enabled precision agriculture, crop and land monitoring, irrigation planning, livestock tracking, and efficient resource management. Research and training in RTK, PPP, CORS, and geospatial data collection contribute to sustainable agricultural practices and improved food security.

cards.title: Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure
cards.description: The Lab advances indigenous capability in GNSS receivers, signal processing, software-defined radio, augmentation systems, integrated navigation, precise positioning, and resilient PNT. Its research infrastructure supports innovation in surveying, telecommunications, transportation, engineering, and critical infrastructure.

cards.title: Sustainable Cities and Communities
cards.description: GNSS technologies developed and studied at the Lab support intelligent transportation, urban planning, cadastral mapping, infrastructure monitoring, emergency response, and smart-city applications. These capabilities contribute to safer, more efficient, and more resilient communities.

cards.title: Climate Action
cards.description: Through GNSS and GISTM observations, the Lab supports ionospheric and tropospheric monitoring, Total Electron Content analysis, space-weather research, crustal deformation studies, flood-risk assessment, and environmental monitoring. These activities strengthen climate resilience and disaster preparedness.

cards.title: Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions
cards.description: The Lab contributes to reliable and resilient PNT capabilities for geospatial governance, emergency services, critical infrastructure protection, national security, and evidence-based decision-making. Research in GNSS integrity, interference mitigation, augmentation, and navigation reliability supports stronger institutional capacity.

comp6.title: Mission
comp6.description: To advance GNSS science and technology through high-quality research, specialised academic programmes, modern infrastructure, collaborative innovation and practical capacity building.

cards.title: Research, Innovation and Technological Development
cards.description: Conduct high-quality research and develop practical GNSS, PNT and space-weather solutions aligned with emerging national and global needs.

cards.title: Education, Capacity Building and Human Capital Development
cards.description: Deliver specialized academic programmes, research supervision and hands-on training that prepare students and professionals for advanced GNSS practice.

cards.title: Collaboration, National Impact and Knowledge Transfer
cards.description: Build productive partnerships, transfer knowledge into applications and contribute to Pakistan's space, geospatial and digital infrastructure.

comp8.title: Team
comp8.description: The lab brings together academic leadership, GNSS specialists, research staff, graduate researchers and technical personnel working across satellite navigation, signal processing, space weather, geodesy and integrated navigation.
